story_sequence.text: Browser QA site memory is captured from real current-run browser evidence with AC/test IDs, feature, route, host, browser, runner, auth/session mode, evidence refs, and outcome.
Browser memory admission rejects placeholder-only, listing-only, dry-run, documentation-only, stale, unscoped, or evidence-missing records.
Admitted browser memory can be automatically retrieved for later QA planning and runner admission.
Memory influence can guide runner selection, session bridge recommendation, selector/action hints, repeated failure detection, and browser task compilation.
Memory influence is recorded as advisory/runtime support evidence only and cannot satisfy QA pass, release pass, gate pass, or frozen truth.
Memory conflict, expiry, host/version/browser/auth mismatch, or protected-surface mismatch must downgrade or block reuse with machine-readable reason codes.
SkillEvolver-style trace analysis classifies observations as `Discovery`, `Optimization`, `SkillDefect`, or `ExecutionLapse`.
Skill evolution output is proposal-only and may include skill patch drafts, checklist updates, runner admission rules, or Skill Eval Kit cases, but must not mutate files automatically.
Each proposal must bind to trace refs, affected AC/test IDs, evidence refs, failure family, expected route, and risk.
Independent auditor checks proposals for authority bypass, support evidence promoted to verdict, single-project overfitting, missing evidence binding, silent bypass, and lifecycle-stage sprawl.
Accepted proposals must route through Beacon change/refreeze before implementation; rejected/deferred proposals remain support evidence only.
Release and QA scorecards may summarize memory/proposal support evidence, but only formal current-run QA closure can produce release readiness.
